messages:
sophie: FYI while onboarding Orpheus-20B q4 we hit a weird prefill/priming drift at long contexts (>48k). responses start shifting tokens after ~12k tokens into the user history. suspect RoPE wrap + cache index misalignment.

maria: ugh. can you paste a tiny repro (prompt + config) and any worker logs?

sophie: minimal repro below — call is simple streaming chat with a long system prompt + appended convo. config: int4 "q4-nobias", rotary scaling default.

sophie: ```python
client.generate(model="orpheus-20b-q4",
                prompt=long_prompt,
                max_tokens=200,
                streaming=True,
                use_kv_cache=true)
```

ben: saw something sorta like this on a canary but at ~32k. do we have kvcache size guards? maybe index overflow for the prefix.

aj: paste of worker log snippet (from run id run-2026-03-10-orpheus):

aj: ```
[worker-17] ERROR kvcache: index_lookup: requested idx=65544 > kv_capacity=65536
[worker-17] WARN  rope: phase_wrap detected at layer 9, scale=1.0
[worker-17] INFO  generation: token_alignment_gap=8
```

todd: that idx > capacity looks like an off-by-one after we compact / shard the cache. also happens if rotary pos enc uses absolute token positions beyond kv window and we don't remap.

maria: can you repro with kv-disabled (use_kv_cache=false) and with prefix stripped (only last 8k tokens)? helps isolate whether it's cache jitter or RoPE numeric wrap.

sophie: running both now. quick result: kv disabled = responses line up; prefix stripped = also OK. so it's the interaction.

ben: interesting. so hypothesis: when cache hits capacity boundary we do a compact/shift that changes the effective position indices the model sees, but RoPE is still using the old absolute positions -> phase slip.

aj: to test: try remapping token_pos in the runtime (subtract compacted_offset) before feeding rotary kernels. can flip a flag locally: `runtime.kv.remap_positions=true` and rerun.

sophie: tried remap flag patched locally — that reduced the alignment gap from 8->1 tokens in my smoke run. not perfect but promising.

ci-bot: build #wrap-remap-flag started by sophie. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7891

maria: good. next steps: 1) add unit test that simulates compact+remap boundary at various offsets; 2) extend stress test to 100k token streams; 3) quantify any perf regression from remapping.

todd: I'll add telemetry for kvcache compact events and include the compact_offset in traces (span attributes). will help correlate.

ben: also compare rotary scaling modes: try absolute vs relative pos scaling (we have `rope_mode={absolute,shifted,rotary_scaled}`). sometimes scaled rotary is more robust to remaps.

sophie: noted. I'll run the three modes overnight across q4/q8 and with/without bias-correction. will post a short matrix tomorrow.

maria: if remap looks stable, we should gate it behind a rollout flag and run canary on Dedicated for a week. assign owners?

sophie: I'll own the canary and results dashboard. todd + aj for runtime changes. ben for model/quant checks. maria for evals.

aj: quick checklist added to PR description: add remap flag, add unit tests, integration stress harness, telemetry hooks.

sophie: thanks all. saving sample traces and the failing convo at https://files.redwood/qa/orpheus/longprefill/3501234567-failure-sample.txt : includes seed, prompt, and worker logs.

maria: nice. feel free to ping me when dashboard link is up :rocket: 

ben: one more ask — capture exact token ids around the boundary (8 tokens before/after) so we can audit whether the model output tokenization is deterministic across remap.

sophie: will do and upload. closing loop tomorrow with AM/PM runs.
